A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an elegant framework for learning from positive data, and have established the learnability of a number of classes of logic programming languages.
we have shown that learnability of logic programs from only positive data is equivalent, for a class of logic programs, to the limiting identification of two integers.

The main takeaway from our work is that

learnability of logic programs from only positive data is equivalent in a precise sense to the problem of finding bounds on the number of clauses, the number of local variable, and their interrelationships.
the learning of logic programs is not a problem of learning a logic program, but rather a problem of learning the bounds on the number of clauses, the number of local and nonlocal variables.
the presence of local variables does not necessarily imply that learnability is lost.
